findings.text: Guest shadow context for nested NPT is prepared from paging plus write protection with selected host protections cleared, a derived CPU role, a nested address walk, a TDP sized root with conditional passthrough when host walk depth differs, and installation of the nested table base.
Nested NPT setup expects a non-direct guest-mode role with paging active and records a host misc control toggle into the SMEP related role flag.

Nested EPT root role is built with caller supplied depth, execute-only and monitoring toggles mapped to role flags, accessed-dirty inverted to a disable flag, full access rights, no short entries, non-direct guest mode, and cleared extension word except execute-only and validity.

Nested EPT initialization derives walk depth from the new table pointer, compares the freshly built role against the stored nested walk role, and only on change refreshes stored roles, fault and translation and sync handlers, permission masks, and reserved-bit masks before installing the new table base.

Guest table entry fetch assumes current paging mode, merges a short PAE write into an aligned wider read, performs atomic guest reads only for two fixed widths, and yields zero on read failure or unsupported length.

Atomic guest read translates address to frame and slot, rejects cross-page ranges and error host mappings, disables faults around an inatomic copy from the host mapping, restores fault state, and maps any copy shortfall to a fault error.
Write flooding detection exempts lowest-level pages, otherwise increments a per-page counter and reports flooding once the count reaches a small fixed threshold.

Misaligned write detection uses entry width from the short-entry flag, exempts aligned single-byte status updates, and otherwise flags writes crossing entry boundaries or shorter than a fixed minimum.

Translation from fault address to shadow entries adjusts page offset for short entries, doubles coverage for legacy narrow roots with rounding cleanup, enforces quadrant match, and otherwise indexes the shadow array for a single entry.

Guest page-table write tracking orders the emulated store before shadowing checks, exits early when no indirect pages exist, fetches the guest entry, walks pages by frame, zaps flooded or misaligned pages with accounting, otherwise zaps affected entries while tracking whether any present entry requires remote action, then performs a combined flush or zap.
Write tracking holds the VM address-space lock in write mode across fetch accounting, page walk, zap preparation, and remote flush or zap completion.

Single-address invalidation for global mappings covers all roots without identifier filtering, while identifier-targeted invalidation selects current and matching previous roots by active and stored identifiers and only acts when at least one root matches; both count an invalidation statistic.

Global MMU configuration stores TDP enablement and root bounds, enables the TDP variant only when both allowed and requested, and selects the maximum huge-page tier from TDP capability when enabled or from host large-page support otherwise.

Per-vCPU MMU creation initializes root state to invalid, empties previous-root records, wires each context to its walk structure, prepares list and header and shadow caches with defined zeroing behavior, selects the primary context, creates guest then root contexts, and releases guest pages if root creation fails.

PAE root table allocation is skipped for the unused guest context without TDP and for TDP modes above legacy extended depth; otherwise a low-memory page is allocated, marked decrypted for shadow paging, warned if unexpected encryption state under TDP, and its fixed slots are poisoned as invalid.

Per-VM MMU setup copies the shared MMIO shadow marker, initializes active and possibly-noncacheable huge-page lists and the unsync lock, chooses TDP MMU initialization or page-hash allocation, and wires split-operation caches for headers, shadow pages, and descriptors with zeroing.

Split-cache readiness also requires absence of scheduling need and lock break need plus minimum free objects in descriptor, header, and shadow caches; topup asserts slot-lock ownership, refills descriptor cache with buffered capacity and the other caches to one, and callers drop and retake the address-space lock around scheduling and topup with a retry signal.

Huge-page splitting for nested use obtains a direct child page for the huge region, populates missing small entries with rmap linkage while preserving existing present entries, requests a flush if an existing non-leaf entry is encountered, links the child, restarts the rmap walk on success or retry, and skips invalid, unsync, non-nested, or non-large cases with warnings for unexpected shapes.

Collapsible-entry reclamation restarts its walk after each zap of a direct page whose frame lies in the slot and whose level is below the host maximum, using ranged remote flush when available else deferring a global flush; full teardown holds write mode, prepares every active page with restart on progress or scheduling, commits the batch, extends to TDP roots when enabled, and then releases.
Splitting aborts with no-space when free MMU pages are at or below the reserved minimum, and creation fails with no-memory when the low-memory root page cannot be allocated.
Batch zap page count is ten.
Diagnostic dump performs a lockless walk for the fault address, returns silently when the walk reports absence, otherwise logs the address plus each shadow entry from root down to leaf.
Slot rmap write protection delegates directly to the generic rmap protector without forcing a flush indicator.
Cache topup need is decided by comparing the cached free-object count against a caller supplied minimum.
